title: Know Your Limits: The Law of Grandiosity
coreMove: Deflate success-driven fantasy by forcing ambition through feedback, constraint, and scale tests before expansion.
sourcePressure: This law keeps ambition and delusion in tension: success, praise, and insulation from feedback swell self-image until proportion fails.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Attacking confidence or ambition instead of showing how lost proportion turns vision reckless.

exampleSpecs.domain: a food-truck owner trying to open three locations after one viral month
exampleSpecs.audience: an operator intoxicated by sudden demand
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether expansion breaks quality and cash
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she places the viral sales chart beside prep-capacity numbers and removes two locations from the plan
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a laminated truck menu beside a white cash-flow printout

exampleSpecs.domain: a university esports captain overruling coaches after a tournament win
exampleSpecs.audience: a young leader confusing momentum with invulnerability
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the team loses discipline before playoffs
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after a loss, he maps every ignored scrim warning against the praise he kept rereading
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a headset on top of a keyboard with worn WASD keys

exampleSpecs.domain: a boutique hotelier adding luxury amenities without fixing plumbing complaints
exampleSpecs.audience: a business owner seduced by image upgrades
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether reputation collapses under basic failures
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he predicts guests will praise the rooftop lounge, then reads reviews that mention water pressure before decor
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a brass room key beside a printed plumbing complaint

exampleSpecs.domain: a medical resident praised for speed who starts skipping checklists
exampleSpecs.audience: a trainee whose identity outruns the system
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the attending asks her to read the missed checklist item aloud before discussing talent
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a surgical checklist clipped to a blue clipboard

exampleSpecs.domain: a local theater director staging an impossible production after one hit
exampleSpecs.audience: an artist who mistakes applause for infinite capacity
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether volunteers burn out and the production fails
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after seeing the build schedule, he cuts the rotating set and keeps the emotional center of the play
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a scale model of a rotating set stuck halfway around

exampleSpecs.domain: a nonprofit founder invited onto panels after a successful pilot
exampleSpecs.audience: a mission leader risking drift into self-mythology
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the organization serves clients or the founder's image
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she compares panel travel days with client waitlist numbers and cancels the trip that feeds reputation more than mission
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a conference lanyard lying across a waitlist spreadsheet

skillTargets: use feedback as a proportion test

tryThisNowSpec: Before expanding one plan, ask the most skeptical qualified person to name the limit you are currently refusing to price.
